SLIDES:
My favourite possession is a ring.

a / an — you mention it for the first time. The listener does not know it yet.

The ring was my grandmother’s.

the — second mention. Now we both know which ring.

It’s got a dark blue stone with a black spot on it.

Two new things, so a twice. Not the — you have not heard about them before.

I love — antique jewellery.

Zero article: plural or uncountable, meaning in general. Not the antique jewellery.

It’s made of — metal, and it’s the only thing I have from her.

Material in general → zero. the only — there is just one, so it must be the.

Warm-up: The limit is the point. Making them drop one is what starts the talking.
Articles arrive in stage 3. Do not correct I choose the phone here.
Vocabulary: leather / metal / plastic are the anchor. The adjectives hang off them.
Audio 5.2 and 5.3 are recognition only. Mark the stress on the board, do not drill production.
Grammar: a/an = new information, the = we both know it, zero = plural or uncountable in general. Everything else is detail.
Russian and Kazakh have no articles, so the default error is omission. Insist on a in It’s a ring.
Practice: Verb patterns from Unit 4. Do not skip it — it is the only place they come back this lesson.
Audio 5.8 gives five sets of adjectives. Play each set twice.
Listening: Play the whole track once, then one speaker at a time. The names are on the recording.
Secondary input. One short task only.
Speaking: Keep them describing. If they drift into why they like it, that is fine, but the article practice is in the description.
Wrap: Verb patterns, Unit 4. Say it out loud.
Lesson 14 is money, and quantity words.

Stage 3 · Grammar

a, the, or nothing at all

Your language does not have articles. English uses one in almost every noun phrase, so this is a habit to build, not a rule to remember.

Read these four sentences from the recording in stage 5.
  • My favourite possession is a ring.
  • The ring was my grandmother’s.
  • It’s got a dark blue stone with a black spot on it.
  • It’s made of — pale grey metal.
Why is it a ring in the first sentence and the ring in the second?
The three-way choice
a / antheno article
Whennew information; one of manywe both know which oneplural or uncountable, in general
ExampleI bought a wallet.The wallet was expensive.I like — wallets.
Also used forjobs: she’s an engineeronly one of its kind: the sun, the best, the onlymaterials: made of — metal
Also used forquantity: a few, a lot ofsaid before: the box I told you aboutmeals, most places: at — home, to — work
a or an?an before a vowel sound: an antique, an hour. But a university, a useful thing — those start with a y sound.
Verb patterns recycledI enjoy collecting old things · I decided to keep it · I can’t imagine living without it
The rules that matter
  • First mention → a / an. After that, the same thing takes the. This one pattern covers most of what you will say.
  • A singular countable noun almost never stands alone. It’s ring is wrong; It’s a ring is right.
  • Plural or uncountable, talking generally → no article: I love — antique jewellery, made of — leather.
  • an or a depends on the sound, not the letter: an hour, a useful tool.
  • You met verb patterns in Unit 4. They come back in task 5 of the next stage.
Full grammar reference — Articles: a / an, the, and no article

Form

a / anone thing, mentioned for the first time: I bought a bag.
an before a vowel soundan hour · an umbrella · but a useful tool, a university
thethe listener knows which one: The bag was expensive.
No articleplurals and uncountables in general: I like — books. · — Money is not everything.
JobsShe is an accountant. — English always uses a / an here.

Spelling and sound

The choice depends on sound, not spelling: an hour (silent h), a university (it starts with a /j/ sound).

When and why we use it

  • First mention takes a / an; after that, the: I saw a man. The man was carrying a box.
  • The is also used when there is only one: the sun, the internet, the first floor, the best film.
  • No article for things in general, and for materials: It is made of — leather.
  • No article with most countries, streets and meals: in — Kazakhstan, on — Abay Street, after — lunch.

Signal words

the same · the only · the first / second · the best — all take the

Watch out — the mistakes learners really make

  • I bought a old wallet. → I bought an old wallet.Vowel sound.
  • She is accountant. → She is an accountant.Jobs take a / an.
  • I like the books. → I like books.Things in general take no article.
  • The money is not everything. → Money is not everything.General idea, no article.

Don’t confuse it with

a introduces; the points at something you have both already agreed on. If your listener could ask ‘which one?’, use a.

Stage 5 · Main input

Five things, one person

The five objects somebody chose, and the reason none of them cost much.

Before you read: a museum asks you to choose five objects from your home that would tell a stranger who you are. Which of these would you look for first?

A prediction, not an answer. Read and see what the writer chose.

Five things, one person

A museum in my city asked people to do something strange: choose five objects from your home that would tell a stranger who you are. Not the most valuable five. The five that mean something. I thought it would take ten minutes. It took me a week.

The first was easy. A green bicycle. Not the green bicycle in the photograph on my wall — that one was stolen — but the plastic-and-metal one I bought to replace it. It is not fashionable and it is certainly not brand new. The condition is terrible. I have ridden it every day for nine years.

Then a leather notebook, heavy, with thin paper and a pale blue cover. I do not write in it. I collect train tickets in it, and the collection is now nearly full.

Then an antique wooden spoon that belonged to my grandmother. It is the only object in the house that is older than my father.

The fourth was a lamp — a shiny, bright, completely useless lamp that a friend gave me. My flat is minimalist because I cannot afford furniture, and the lamp is the one thing in it that argues with the walls.

The fifth took the rest of the week. In the end I chose a key. It opens a door in a city I no longer live in, and it is not suitable for anything now, but I have never been able to throw it away.

Here is what surprised me. Nothing on my list was expensive, and nothing was essential. Ask somebody what possessions they own and they will tell you about money. Ask them for five objects and they will tell you about their life.

Note. Written for this course as a reading text, in the first person. The museum project and the writer are invented; the idea — a personal collection chosen for meaning rather than value — is the one behind the time-capsule and ‘object stories’ projects that museums run. No words are attributed to a real person.
